title: Crossing Midnight
description: The same shipment can land in a different calendar day depending on which timezone the report is viewed in — a shipment booked just after UTC midnight might still be "yesterday" on the US West Coast. Prove the bucketing genuinely shifts with the timezone, not just the label.
successCondition: Book a shipment at a moment you control precisely (or find one) whose UTC timestamp is between 00:00 and 03:00 UTC. GET /api/reporting/summary with groupBy=day, timeZone=UTC, and a from/to window covering that day shows the shipment counted in the UTC calendar date's bucket. The same query with timeZone=America/Los_Angeles (UTC-7 or UTC-8 depending on DST) over the same absolute from/to window shows the shipment counted in the previous calendar date's bucket instead — a genuinely different period string.
hints: You likely can't control a shipment's createdAt directly through the API — instead, time your booking request to actually happen within the 00:00-03:00 UTC window, or pick a from/to window and timezone combination based on when you're actually running the test.
docs/api/reporting.md and bucketing.ts confirm this cross-timezone bucket shift is intentional behavior, not a bug — the test is proving the intentional behavior holds, not reporting it as a defect.
